blocks.content: Not every lock puts a waiting thread to sleep. A spinlock keeps it running, burning CPU cycles in a tight loop until the lock becomes free.
1. What a Spinlock Is
A spinlock is a lock where a thread that finds it already held does not go to sleep. Instead, it busy waits: it repeatedly checks the lock in a tight loop, spinning, until the lock is released.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785408560075-448701648.png
2. The Critical Contrast With a Mutex
blocks.text: 2. The Critical Contrast With a Mutex

blocks.content: This is the single most important thing to understand about spinlocks. A mutex blocks a waiting thread, putting it to sleep so the OS scheduler can run something else useful on that CPU core in the meantime.
A spinlock keeps the waiting thread actively running the whole time it waits, consuming CPU the entire duration, whether or not it ends up doing anything useful with that time.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785408560075-337955275.png
blocks.alt: The Critical Contrast With a Mutex

blocks.content: 3. Why Anyone Would Want Busy Waiting
blocks.text: 3. Why Anyone Would Want Busy Waiting

blocks.content: Putting a thread to sleep and waking it back up later is not free, it costs a context switch. If the expected wait is very short, shorter than a context switch itself would take, spinning can actually finish faster overall than sleeping.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785408560075-469636006.png
blocks.alt: Why Anyone Would Want Busy Waiting

blocks.content: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785408560075-282457996.png
blocks.alt: Why Anyone Would Want Busy Waiting

blocks.content: 4. The Single Core Danger

Spinlocks are genuinely dangerous on a single core system. If a thread is spinning waiting for a lock, and the thread that holds it cannot run because the one available core is entirely occupied by the spinning thread, the lock can never be released.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785408657684-433713175.png

blocks.title: This is a guaranteed deadlock
blocks.content: The spinning thread never yields the CPU, so the holder never gets scheduled, so the lock is held forever.
5. Where Spinlocks Are Actually Used
In practice, spinlocks live mostly deep inside operating system kernels, protecting very short, predictable critical sections like a small piece of kernel data.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785408657685-480394825.png
Application level code almost never should reach for a spinlock directly. That decision is normally left to the kernel or a well tested library that already accounts for the risks above.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785408657686-104490406.png

7. A Minimal Implementation
The core building block is an atomic test and set instruction, one CPU operation that reads the old value and sets a new one without any other thread able to interleave in between.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785408657686-92259463.png
8. Common Mistakes

["Using a spinlock for a long or unpredictable critical section, wasting enormous amounts of CPU time.","Using a spinlock in ordinary application code where a standard mutex would be both simpler and safer."]
items: Using a spinlock for a long or unpredictable critical section, wasting enormous amounts of CPU time.
Using a spinlock in ordinary application code where a standard mutex would be both simpler and safer.

blocks.content: 9. Interview Angle

The busy wait versus sleep distinction is a common, sharp follow up question after discussing mutexes. Being able to explain when spinning is actually the right tradeoff, not just that it exists, is what signals real understanding.
